request: Implement a persistent profile service. Commands: create {id,name} returns {ok:true}; get {id} returns exactly {id,name}; rename {id,name} returns {ok:true}; delete {id} returns {ok:true}. IDs are positive integers, names nonempty strings; invalid input returns {error:"invalid"}. Missing profiles return {error:"not_found"}; duplicate IDs return {error:"conflict"}. Never expose raw database errors. Parameterize SQL. Data survives service restart.
private_setup_sql: CREATE TABLE profiles(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL);

request: Implement commands balance {id} -> {id,balance}, and transfer {from,to,amount} -> {ok:true}. IDs and amount must be positive integers; from!=to, otherwise {error:"invalid"}. Debit source then credit destination in one transaction, using row locks. Missing accounts: {error:"not_found"}; inadequate source balance: {error:"insufficient"}; unexpected database failure: {error:"db_error"}. Any failure rolls back both changes. Parameterize SQL.
transaction_requirements: Debit and credit are atomic; callback errors and database errors roll back all writes.

private_cases.sql: SELECT balance FROM wallets ORDER BY id;
SELECT balance FROM wallets ORDER BY id;
SELECT balance FROM wallets WHERE id=1;

request: Implement signup {id,email} -> {ok:true}, where id positive integer and email nonempty string. Insert into registrations then signup_events using the same id and email in one transaction. Duplicate id/email -> {error:"conflict"}, invalid input -> {error:"invalid"}, unexpected database failure -> {error:"db_error"}. Any failure leaves neither a partial registration nor a partial event. Parameterize SQL.
transaction_requirements: Registration and audit insertion must use the same transaction and roll back together.

private_cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM registrations; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signup_events;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM registrations; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signup_events;

request: Implement batch {entries:[{id,value},...]} -> {written:N}, and count -> {count:N}. Entries must be nonempty; IDs positive integers and values nonempty strings; invalid input -> {error:"invalid"}. Insert entries sequentially in one transaction. Duplicate IDs, including duplicates later in the same batch, return {error:"conflict"} and roll back the entire batch. Parameterize SQL; data survives restart.
transaction_requirements: All entries share one transaction; a later insert failure rolls back earlier inserts.
private_setup_sql: CREATE TABLE notes(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,value VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL);

request: Implement reserve {items:[{id,quantity},...]} -> {ok:true}, and stock {id} -> {id,qty}. Item IDs/quantities must be positive integers; no duplicate item IDs; items nonempty, otherwise {error:"invalid"}. Lock and decrement stocks in one transaction. Missing SKU -> {error:"not_found"}; inadequate stock -> {error:"insufficient"}; failure rolls back every decrement. Parameterize SQL.
transaction_requirements: Reservations are atomic across all requested SKU updates.
private_setup_sql: CREATE TABLE stocks(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,qty BIGINT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO stocks VALUES(7,5),(8,2);

private_cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM stocks ORDER BY id;
SELECT qty FROM stocks ORDER BY id;

request: Implement create_order {id,lines:[{id,sku,quantity},...]} -> {id,line_count:N}. All numeric fields positive integers, lines nonempty; invalid -> {error:"invalid"}. Insert orders row (status="created") then all order_lines rows, each referring to the parent id, in one transaction. Duplicate order or line IDs -> {error:"conflict"}; any failure rolls back parent and all lines. Parameterize SQL.
transaction_requirements: Parent and all child rows must commit or roll back together.
private_setup_sql: CREATE TABLE orders(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,status VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE order_lines(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,order_id BIGINT NOT NULL,sku BIGINT NOT NULL,quantity INT NOT NULL,FOREIGN KEY(order_id) REFERENCES orders(id));

private_cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_lines;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_lines;
